questions.question: If sum of ₹8,000 invested at 10% per annum interest compounded half-yearly, amounts to ₹9,261, then what is the time period?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum = Rs. 8000 

Rate of interest = 10% p.a = 5% half-yearly

Amount = Rs. 9261

**Formula used:**

A = P × [1 + (R/100)]t

**Calculation:**

⇒ 9261 = 8000 × [1 + (5/100)]t

⇒ 9261/8000 = (21/20)t

⇒ (21/20)³ = (21/20)t

⇒ t = 3 half-year

**∴ Time is 1(1)/(2) years.**

questions.question: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 8. If A and B spend ₹36,000 and ₹60,000, respectively, then the ratio of their savings is 3 : 4. What is the savings (in ₹) of B?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Income ratio of A and B = 5x : 8x

Savings ratio of A and B = 3 : 4

Spend (Expenditure) of A and B = 36000 and 60000 respectively,

**Formula used:**

Income - Expenditure = Saving.

**Calculation:**

⇒ (5x - 36000) / (8x - 60000) = 3 : 4 

⇒ 4 × (5x - 36000) = 3 × (8x - 60000)

⇒ 20x - 144000 = 24x - 180000

⇒ 4x = 36000

⇒ x = 9000

Savings of B = (8x - 60000)

⇒ 8 × 9000 - 60000 = 12000

**∴ Savings of B = 12000**

questions.question: If the LCM of four distinct numbers is 270 and the HCF of each pair is 9, then what is the product of the four numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the four numbers be 9a, 9b, 9c, and 9d (where a, b, c, d are pairwise coprime).

LCM = 9 × a × b × c × d = 270

⇒ a × b × c × d = 30

Product of the numbers = (9a) × (9b) × (9c) × (9d) = 9⁴ × (abcd)

⇒ Product = 6561 × 30 = 196830

**∴ The correct answer is 196830.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ LCM of four distinct numbers = 270

⇒ HCF of each pair = 9

 Four Distinct Numbers (HCF = 9)
 
 
 9 × 1
 9
 
 
 9 × 2
 18
 
 
 9 × 3
 27

 
 9 × 5
 45

 
• 
 
 LCM = 9 × (1 × 2 × 3 × 5) = 270
 Product = 9 × 18 × 27 × 45 = 196830

**Calculation:**

⇒ Since the HCF of each pair is 9, all four distinct numbers must be multiples of 9.

⇒ Let the four numbers be 9a, 9b, 9c, and 9d, where a, b, c, and d are pairwise coprime integers.

⇒ The LCM of these four numbers is evaluated as = 9 × a × b × c × d

⇒ 9abcd = 270

⇒ abcd = 30

⇒ The only four distinct positive pairwise coprime integers whose product evaluates to 30 are 1, 2, 3, and 5.

⇒ Thus, the four numbers are: 9 × 1 = 9, 9 × 2 = 18, 9 × 3 = 27, and 9 × 5 = 45.

⇒ Product of the four numbers = 9 × 18 × 27 × 45

⇒ Product = 196830

**∴ The correct answer is 196830.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM & HCF of Two Numbers

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers is strictly equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (i.e., a × b = HCF × LCM). However, this direct rule is generally not applicable to three or more numbers.

Pairwise Coprime Numbers

A set of numbers is pairwise coprime if any given pair chosen from the set has an HCF of exactly 1. The LCM of a set of pairwise coprime numbers is always equal to their product.

Multiples of HCF

If the HCF of a set of numbers is H, every number in the set can be factorized as H × k, where k represents distinct integers that do not possess any mutual common factors across the overall group.

questions.question: By selling an article for ₹460, Sudha loses 8%. If she sells it for ₹590, then her profit percentage is :
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The first SP of the article = Rs. 460

Loss = 8%

The second SP = Rs. 590

**Formula used:**

CP = SP × 100/(100 - L%)

P% = P × 100/CP

**Calculation:**

⇒ CP = 460 × 100/(100 - 8)

⇒ 460 × 100/92 = 460 × 50/46 = 500

⇒ CP = Rs. 500

When SP = Rs. 590

⇒ Profit = 590 - 500 = 90

⇒ Profit % = 90 × 100/500 = 18

**Hence profit will be 18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** When loss is 8% SP is Rs. 460

⇒ 460 = 92%

⇒ 1 = 1/5

⇒ 590 = (1/5)590 = 118

⇒ SP is 118% of CP

**∴ Profit is 18%**

questions.question: By selling an article at 9over11 of its selling price, Madhu incurs a loss of 10%. If she sells the article at 95% of its actual selling price, then what is the profit percentage (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

SP₂ = 9/11 of the actual SP and Loss = 10%

**Formula used:**

CP = SP × 100/(100 - L%)

P% = P × 100/CP

Where CP = cost price, SP = selling price

And P = profit

**Calculation:**

Let the actual SP be 11x then SP₂ = 9x

Now loss is 10%, therefore

⇒ CP = 9x × 100 /(100 - 10)

⇒ CP = 9x × 100/90 = 10x

Let SP₃ be 95% of the actual SP

⇒ SP₃ = 95% of 11x = 10.45x

Now profit = 10.45x - 10x = 0.45x

⇒ Profit% = 0.45x × 100/10x = 4.5

**Hence, the required profit is 4.5%.**

questions.question: The compound interest on a sum of ₹8,400 in 3 years at a certain rate percent per annum is ₹6115.20, interest being compounded annually. What will be the difference in (₹) between compound interest on the same sum at the same rate for 1{1 over 2} years, when the interest is compounded half yearly and the simple interest on the same sum for same rate and for the same period?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 8400, Time Period = 3 years

Compound Interest = Rs. 6115.20

**Formula used:**

Compound Interest = P × [1 + (R/100)]ⁿ - P

Simple Interest = [P × R × T]/100

Where P = Principal, R = Rate of interest, n = Time in years

**Calculation:**

According to the Question,

Compound Interest = P × [1 + (R/100)]n - P

⇒ 6115.20 = 8400 × (1 + R/100)³ - 8400

⇒ 6115.20 + 8400 = 8400[((100 + R)/100)³]

⇒ 14515.20/8400 = [(100 + R)/100]³

⇒ 1728/1000 = [(100 + R)/100]3 

⇒ [(100 + R)/100] = (1728/1000)¹/³

⇒ [(100 + R)/100] = 12/10

⇒ R = 20%

Compound interest for 1{1 over 2} years, when compounded half-yearly

∴ R = 20/2 = 10%, and T = 3 years

Compound Interest = P × [1 + (R/100)]n - P

⇒ 8400 × [(100 + 10%)/100]³ - 8400

⇒ 8400[(110/100)³ - 1]

⇒ 8400 × 331/1000 = 2780.4

Simple Interest on the same sum for the same rate and time,

⇒ Simple Interest = [P × R × T]/100

⇒ [8400 × 20 × (3/2)]/100 = 2520

The required difference = 2780.4 - 2520 = 260.4

**∴ Hence the required difference is ₹ 260.4**

questions.question: A cylindrical vessel of base radius 10.5 cm and height 30 cm is 4 over5 full of water. The entire water is poured into a rectangular tub of length 44 cm and breadth 36 cm. The height (in cm) to which the water level rises in the tub is (Take pi = {22 over 7} ) (Assuming no overflow of water)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radius (r) = 10.5 cm and Height (h) = 30 cm

The cylindrical vessel is 4 over5 full of water

Length of the rectangular tube, l = 44 cm

The breadth of the rectangular tube, b = 36 cm

**Formula used: **

The volume of the cylindrical vessel = π r²h

The volume of the rectangular tube = l × b × h

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb5d5a94b29cd240bb396d9ecbeecd4f896d319997609fe2159fa6e24ff954f6.png] 

The volume of the cylindrical vessel = π r2h

⇒ 22over7 × 10.5 × 10.5 × 30 = 10395 cm³

The cylindrical vessel is 4 over5 full of water, therefore

⇒ Volume = 4 over5 × 10395 = 8316

The volume of the rectangular tube = 8316

⇒ l × b × h = 8316

⇒ 44 × 36 × h = 8316

⇒ h = {8316}over{44×36} = 5 {1 over 4} cm

**∴ The height to the water level rises in the tub is 5 {1 over 4} cm.**
